title: LEAF: Lightweight and Efficient Hardware Accelerator for Signature Verification of FALCON
problem: FALCON signature verification is computationally complex, and existing hardware accelerators only target high-performance scenarios, leaving resource-constrained applications without efficient implementations.
motivation: Post-quantum cryptography (NIST-standardized FALCON) requires efficient hardware acceleration for resource-constrained embedded systems.
method: LEAF proposes an efficient design strategy with novel data dependence flow to maximize small-resource utilization, an ultra-lightweight number theoretical transform (NTT) core with novel twiddle factor access pattern, targeting signature verification only.
key_novelty: Novel data dependence flow and twiddle factor access pattern enabling resource-efficient FALCON signature verification without sacrificing throughput.
contributions: Novel data dependence flow maximizing small-resource utilization for all arithmetic procedures
Ultra-lightweight NTT core with novel twiddle factor access pattern
First lightweight full-hardware FALCON signature verification accelerator
65-66% less aggregate resource usage and 24-14% less area-time product versus state-of-the-art

metrics.area: 65-66% less aggregate resource usage; 24-14% less equivalent area-time product (eATP)

limitations: Focuses on signature verification only; key generation and signing procedures not addressed.
